analysis:
The PR adds one documentation row to docs/reference/configuration.md at head line 313 (the patch is truncated at the end of the excerpt, and the head text unit I received ends at line 311). The row documents DARKBLOOM_TTFT_FUSED_CAUSAL_PREFILL, an exact `0`-disables switch that defaults to on and is read once per process. It covers full-attention prompt chunks that take a single fused causal SDPA call on either KV backend, with live packed paged KV excluded. The row says it is not forwarded to LaunchAgents.

This is a documentation-only change, so no code, authorization, attestation, encryption or wire behavior is modified. I checked it against the threat model (TB-007, T-041 and the prefix-cache entries). The doc does not alter any prefix-cache gate, TTL, HMAC lookup-key derivation, salt scoping or disk-budget policy that T-041 designates as sign-off-sensitive.

The fused-prefill setting is a compute-path kernel choice. It does not change what plaintext is retained, cache scoping, or the attested-code boundary. The variable is operator-environment only, as with other foreground-only variables, so no new remote or consumer-controllable attack surface is documented. It is not forwarded to the installed daemon. That means an operator could set it only in a foreground process, which is already within the operator-trust model of T-013 and T-014.

Open question for a later pass: whether the underlying code change (AttentionV1.swift fused causal path) is present in this PR or an earlier one. That code is not in the supplied units. It could affect numerical correctness or memory use in TB-007, but there is no evidence of a security impact. The backend/platform pinned links and the other configuration rows are unchanged context.

No findings.
